assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, proglucagon processing, the active GLP-1(7-36) form) led to therapies that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. Combines clear mechanism with very large clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst established the physiology of GLP-1 and its insulinotropic action, Drucker the biology of GLP-1 and GLP-2 and the translational path, Mojsov the identification and synthesis of the active peptide. Knudsen's industrial engineering of long-acting analogues is major, and Habener is not on this list, so a three-person cap forces a hard choice and credit for the active peptide is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed over decades, and outcome trials and wide clinical adoption are robust. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Priority dispute over the active GLP-1 peptide (Mojsov versus others).
Whether to credit the physiological discovery or the drug-engineering stage.
I am relying on my own recollection of the history and have not verified it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells as living drugs produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemia and lymphoma and opened a new therapeutic modality. The concept is original and the impact is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T cells, Sadelain the CD28-costimulated CAR design and preclinical proof, June the first clinical CD19 CAR-T success with 4-1BB. Other contributors (Eshhar, Kuwana, Gross, Brenner) are not in the credited names, so any trio omits significant work.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and a decade of follow-up establish the clinical effect. Remaining limits are in solid tumours and toxicity, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Credit among the CAR designers is contested.
Limited efficacy in solid tumours and long-term safety such as secondary malignancy.
Based on recalled history, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics transformed experimental neuroscience and physiology by allowing causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with light. It is a widely adopted foundational tool and its use is spreading to cardiac and retinal work.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterised channelrhodopsins, Deisseroth and Boyden built the neuronal toolkit, and Miesenböck made an earlier genetically targeted photoactivation demonstration. Bamberg is also central. Six credited names exceed the cap, so any trio is a contestable selection.
assessment.maturity: The tool has been adopted for around two decades and is independently validated. Clinical translation is early, though partial vision restoration has been reported.
uncertainties: Allocation among six strong contributors is unresolved.
The benefit is mainly a research tool and clinical impact is still limited.
Based on recalled history, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING is the central cytosolic DNA-sensing pathway of innate immunity, with a second-messenger cGAMP, and it bears on infection, autoimmunity, autoinflammation and cancer immunity. It is a clear mechanistic discovery of broad significance.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP, and Barber identified STING. Ishikawa and others contributed to early STING work, and Sun and Wu were part of Chen's discovery team. Two laureates can capture the core pathway.
assessment.maturity: The pathway is confirmed independently and extended widely. Therapeutic translation is still early, and the prize may be somewhat premature on clinical impact, though the basic mechanism is mature.
uncertainties: Clinical translation has not yet matured.
Credit division between the Chen and Barber contributions and the role of other early groups.
Based on recalled history, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined how the endoplasmic reticulum communicates with the nucleus. It has a clean discovery arc (Ire1, Hac1 and XBP1 splicing) and underpins our understanding of proteostasis, secretory-cell biology, diabetes and neurodegeneration.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori made the decisive discoveries, namely Ire1 signalling and unconventional splicing of HAC1 and the identification of the pathway components. Credit would also need to consider Ron and Kaufman's work on other arms, and Walter and Mori form a coherent pair.
assessment.maturity: The work has decades of confirmation and the principles are stable. Disease-relevant translation (ISRIB, PERK inhibitors) is still in development, although basic significance is established.
uncertainties: Other arms of the UPR (PERK, ATF6) have separate contributors not credited here.
Direct clinical translation remains limited.
Based on recalled history, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, a disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, an RNA-based mechanism-to-medicine story with transformative clinical effects in infants.
assessment.attribution: Krainer elucidated the splicing mechanism and the target sequence, and Bennett led development of the antisense chemistry and the drug. This is a concise and fair two-person configuration, with Hua and Singh as contributors who are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term follow-up and a generalisable antisense platform. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with other SMA therapy modalities (gene therapy, risdiplam).
Contribution of other lab members is not recognised.
Based on recalled history, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cell survival, not only proliferation, drives cancer and gave the basis for BH3 mimetics such as venetoclax. A fundamental discovery connected to an approved targeted therapy.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams cloned and characterised the Bcl-2 family biology and its role in lymphoma, and Vaux showed its function as an anti-death gene. Strasser is another major contributor. Credit with Korsmeyer, Tsujimoto and Green not listed among the names is complex.
assessment.maturity: The field is mature, with extensive confirmation and clinical use in CLL and AML. Part of the story is already recognised through the 2002 Nobel on programmed cell death and earlier awards.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier apoptosis recognition.
Contested credit for the original BCL2 translocation discovery.
Based on recalled history, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib showed that inhibiting a defined oncogenic kinase can turn a fatal cancer into a manageable chronic disease, the proof-of-principle for targeted cancer therapy.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the chemistry and discovery of the inhibitor, Druker led the clinical development and preclinical demonstration, and Sawyers contributed resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors. This is a plausible trio, but the underlying discovery of BCR-ABL (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore) is not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of clinical outcome data. It was recognised by Lasker and other awards, and the timing is late but valid. The conceptual breakthrough is established.
uncertainties: The discovery relies on prior work on the Philadelphia chromosome and ABL not credited here.
The roles of industry scientists make the allocation sensitive.
